scope: deterministic non-release project scaffolds, explicit opt-in materialization of port-owned implemented adapter contracts, mandatory execution-role-matched pre-runtime payloads and immutable framework build sources for ARMv7 and AArch64
method: M19 generates invariant delivery files, selects exact NXExtract UI and NXSplash artifacts by their declared execution roles, emits explicit non-release placeholders by default, and materializes selected framework components from verified immutable Git objects before compilation. An explicit promotion copies a coherent adapter contract and claims supplied by the port; it does not execute a game, infer an adapter lifecycle or create physical evidence.

guarantees: the visible wrapper is rendered from the embedded canonical nxport manifest
limitations: the generated wrapper proves structure, not target runtime
tests: both example projects contain the expected launcher

guarantees: the single visible launcher remains generated, declarative and directly loads nxbootstrap without a run.sh layer
limitations: engine preparation remains adapter-owned
tests: shell syntax and line-count gates run on both ABIs

guarantees: nxbootstrap bytes, version and SHA-256 are frozen in each generation receipt
limitations: a later bootstrap change requires regenerating the scaffold
tests: vendored bootstrap is compared byte-for-byte with the canonical source

guarantees: active NXExtract projects receive the complete pinned 1.2.18 engine, the separately pinned immutable 1.2.16 low-glibc UI selected by the extractor role (or the legacy game architecture) and exact recipe; container recipes cannot bind compatibility to one APK hash and may rely on strong internal SHA or structural anchors
limitations: the generator validates recipe shape but does not prove game-specific extraction
tests: all four runtime/UI files and the recipe are byte-compared; Angry Birds, Retro Highway and transformed-container ScourgeBringer policy snapshots remain accepted

guarantees: without an explicit promotion the adapter skeleton begins non-release with empty lifecycle, JNI, persistence and terminal contracts; promotion only materializes a coherent port-owned implemented contract
limitations: game-specific adapter implementation and physical evidence remain port-owned and are never inferred by the generator
tests: the gate preserves the default scaffold and proves deterministic promotion plus fail-closed schema, path, claim and contract mismatches

guarantees: PortMaster metadata v4 names the ZIP, launcher, port directory, ABI and glibc floor, omits attr.runtime only for a validated empty project list, preserves nonempty lists and is pinned to the real current and legacy parser contract
limitations: art, genres and release prose remain deliberate release inputs
tests: metadata is compared to the exact expected ARMHF and AArch64 objects; two generated ZIPs pass the pinned real HarbourMaster cycle; missing, null, scalar and duplicate runtime values fail

guarantees: two clean generations have identical paths, modes and bytes, with every artifact ordered by its complete POSIX logical path
limitations: external compiler output is governed separately by M17
tests: both architecture examples are generated twice and snapshotted; prefix boundaries for hyphen, dot, slash, digit and case remain strictly lexical

guarantees: separate canonical examples cover AArch64, ARMv7/ARMHF and explicit AArch64-extractor plus ARMHF-splash/game mixed execution
limitations: examples contain no proprietary payload or engine behavior
tests: the same generator gate validates both examples

guarantees: the public documentation skeleton contains English and Portuguese sections
limitations: a finished game must replace scaffold text with reviewed facts
tests: generated READMEs must contain both language structures

guarantees: the template follows the approved GTASA presentation categories
limitations: GTASA technical values are never copied as project defaults
tests: section tokens are checked without importing game behavior

guarantees: architecture and actually solved problems have dedicated sections
limitations: the scaffold refuses to invent solved problems
tests: English and Portuguese section pairs are mandatory

guarantees: controls, data, build/run, source map and licenses are explicit
limitations: content remains project-owned and evidence-backed
tests: all presentation sections and local links are checked

guarantees: private address and personal-path literals are rejected or absent from generated public text
limitations: final human-authored prose must still pass nxrelease privacy scanning
tests: hostile title and generated README privacy regressions are exercised

guarantees: Mali-450/GLES2 baseline is separate from an empty proven-support list
limitations: only later exact-ZIP device acceptance may populate support
tests: non-empty generated support declarations are rejected

guarantees: correct opt-in quirks and incorrect global defaults are contrasted bilingually
limitations: no quirk is enabled by the generator
tests: nxport examples retain an empty enabled_quirks array

guarantees: real PortMaster is the release path and direct bootstrap calls are development-only
limitations: host generation does not perform a PortMaster device acceptance
tests: the distinction is required in both language sections

guarantees: support requires the same ZIP and SHA-256 across declared families
limitations: the generator receipt is not a device receipt
tests: same-artifact wording is part of the generated documentation gate

guarantees: the live framework and public indexes route new work through nxgenerator
limitations: the archive master plan remains read-only
tests: canonical local links are resolved by the closure gate

guarantees: generated documentation links and documented shell files are validated
limitations: external web targets are not contacted by offline gates
tests: local link existence and bash syntax are checked offline

guarantees: the original twenty scaffold requirements are machine-accounted and fail closed
limitations: M19 closure does not imply a finished game adapter or physical release
tests: the dedicated closure gate validates schema, evidence and safety claims

guarantees: framework build inputs are materialized only from full immutable Git commits after commit, tree and blob identities, component VERSION and canonical tree SHA-256 are verified
component working trees, replace refs, inherited Git redirection, clean/smudge filters and lazy fetching cannot change pinned source bytes
limitations: ports adopt the build pin by opt-in and must compile exclusively from the published snapshot mounted read-only; historical release pins are not reinterpreted
NXExtract remains separately vendored and pinned, and physical game acceptance is outside this host gate
tests: synthetic commits, dirty checkout, corrupted objects, replace refs, Git environment redirection, filters, lazy fetch, path/umask/locale variance, symlink/gitlink/hardlink, nanosecond mtime, receipt tamper, limits, no-overwrite and a real previous-tag smoke are exercised

guarantees: every new ARMv7 or AArch64 scaffold contains exactly the immutable splash-role-matched nxsplash helper at mode 0755 and records its release manifest, source, artifact ABI and SHA-256
the generated launcher runs that helper after payload validation and before adapter hooks, private libraries and the native game process, with no per-port removal switch
limitations: existing ports remain byte-identical until an explicit migration pins this component
the scaffold gate proves helper identity and ordering but physical rendering remains a same-ZIP device acceptance requirement
tests: both architecture generations compare helper bytes and receipts exactly, while missing, altered, stripped and misordered splash fixtures fail closed
